source.section: PDF p11 'State court judges who were appointed prior to January 2, 1975 receive taxable noncontributory pensions'; PDF p10 Line 4 first bullet (contributory only); Form 1 lines 2a, 2c, 4, 10-22

worked: Federal AGI = Massachusetts noncontributory pension (state judge appointed before January 2, 1975) 40,000.00 (person 0) = 40,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - 17,750.00 standard deduction (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 or older) = 22,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 40,000.00 Massachusetts noncontributory pension (state judge appointed before January 2, 1975) (taxed: noncontributory, outside the exemption, PDF p11 judges paragraph) = 40,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 40,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 40,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (single) = 4,400.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 1 x 700.00 = 700.00; line 2g = line 18 = 5,100.00. Line 19 = 40,000.00 - 5,100.00 = 34,900.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 34,900.00. Line 22 = 34,900.00 x 0.05 = 1,745.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 1,745.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 40,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 1,745.00.
